title: Do Small Models Have Honesty Heads?
tools: PyTorch · Qwen3.5 (0.8B, 2B, 4B) · activation steering · integrated gradients · Slurm on the OSU (Oregon State University) cluster
blurb: A replication of honesty-head steering on three small Qwen3.5 models; a null result, since the one large effect just pushed the model to say Yes.
long: An open method (SauersML/honesty-heads, run on Qwen3.5-9B) finds attention heads and MLP (multilayer perceptron) neurons whose activity separates honest from deceptive answers in role-play prompts, then steers them to remove lies. I wondered if it also worked in Qwen3.5-0.8B, 2B and 4B, so I used their role-play items and their code unmodified.

The upstream labels are from 9B responses, manually labeled. I had each small model generate responses (one greedy and 6 sampled per item, 98 items) and had all responses read and labeled as either a lie, true, or other. If the greedy response and at least one sampled response disagreed, the item was kept. This resulted in 14–16 held-out test lies for each model. The direction is the average activation difference between true and lie items. The heads/neurons are ranked by integrated gradients, then the selected groups are tested on held-out items compared to random groups of the same size.

Result: no unit set clearly carries honesty. Steering all heads fails to outperform random directions on 0.8B and 2B. On 4B, steering all heads reduces 6 out of 14 lies, compared to a maximum of 5 out of 14 for random directions. The selected heads reduce 3, 2, and 4 lies respectively, which is close to the performance of the random control directions.

The fixed-strength neurons were the only results that were clearly outside the range of the controls: 16 neurons removed 11 out of 14 lies on 0.8B, and 147 neurons removed 5 out of 14 on 4B. When we split them up by answer polarity, we can see why. The 0.8B set removes all 10 of the lies where the lie is “No” but only 1 of the other 4, so it is acting as “say Yes”. The 4B set is more “say No”. These are answer-polarity shifts, not honesty. The random neuron controls are also lower perform

ing than a random direction on the same neurons, so their score of 0 overestimates how unusual these sets are.
highlights: Three model sizes, 14-16 held-out lies each, against random controls
Heads: at or near random controls on all three models
0.8B neurons remove 11 of 14 lies, but all 10 "No" lies and 1 of 4 others: a "say Yes" push
Engine check: the method's forward pass matches Hugging Face's within 0.03 nats
